content.user_title: Add Typed Events to React Feeds
content.value_statement: Adding feed events often requires coordinated TypeScript, React, rendering, and WebSocket changes. This skill provides a focused workflow that follows existing project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the existing EventType union and feed block components.
Defines a typed interface for a new feed event.
Adds the event interface to the existing TypeScript union.
Creates a React block component using established project patterns.
Connects the event to feed rendering and relevant WebSocket handling.
Guides validation with a mock WebSocket event.
limitations: Assumes the feed types and components are located in frontend/src/App.tsx.
Provides a workflow and examples, not reusable implementation files.
Does not define backend event production or transport protocols.
Requires project-specific decisions for fields, styling, and rendering behavior.

use_cases.description: Add a typed search result event and render its details in the frontend feed.

use_cases.title: Surface Agent Progress

use_cases.title: Standardize Error Events
use_cases.description: Introduce a structured error event and connect it to existing feed rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a new [event_name] event type with fields for [field_list]. Follow the existing feed component patterns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create one straightforward event type and block.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Styled Event Block
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [event_name] event and React block. Reuse nearby Tailwind styles and explain each changed file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add an event that needs project-consistent presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a WebSocket Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [event_name] across TypeScript types, feed rendering, and WebSocket handling. Include a mock event for validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Implement an event received from the backend.

prompt_templates.title: Extend the Feed End to End
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect existing feed patterns, then add [event_name] with [field_list]. Update types, rendering, transport handling, and focused tests without using any.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate a complete event integration with strict typing.

output_examples.input: Add a progress update event with a message and completion percentage.
output: Added a typed progress event with message and percentage fields.
Created a progress block that follows the existing feed styling.
Connected the event to feed rendering and prepared a mock validation case.

output_examples.input: Create a feed block for structured errors.
output_examples.output: Added a structured error event and matching block, then connected it to the feed renderer using existing naming and styling conventions.

output_examples.input: Display search results received through WebSocket.
output_examples.output: Extended the event union, added a search results block, updated message handling, and described a focused mock event test.

best_practices: Review nearby event interfaces and blocks before making changes.
Keep event names in snake case and React component names in PascalCase.
Test rendering with representative mock WebSocket events.
anti_patterns: Do not use any when a concrete event interface can be defined.
Do not add a union member without connecting its rendering path.
Do not introduce unrelated styles when existing Tailwind patterns are suitable.

faq.question: What files does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects event types and feed components in frontend/src/App.tsx, but the workflow can guide equivalent structures elsewhere.

faq.question: Does it create the backend event?
faq.answer: No. It can update frontend handling for a backend event, but backend production remains project-specific.

faq.question: Can it add WebSocket handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs updates to the message handler when the backend sends the new event type.

faq.question: Does it support strict TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The guardrails require complete types and prohibit any.

faq.question: Will the new block match existing styles?
faq.answer: The workflow reviews nearby blocks and reuses existing Tailwind classes for visual consistency.

faq.question: How should the new event be tested?
faq.answer: Send a representative mock event through the WebSocket path and verify its rendered block and fields.
